facts: The paper explores a new theory of discourse structure.
The theory stresses the role of purpose and processing in discourse.
Discourse structure is composed of three separate but interrelated components.
The structure of the sequence of utterances is called the linguistic structure.
A structure of purposes is called the intentional structure.
The state of focus of attention is called the attentional state.
The linguistic structure consists of segments of the discourse.
The intentional structure captures the discourse-relevant purposes.
The intentional structure captures relationships among linguistic segments.
The attentional state is an abstraction of the focus of attention of the participants.
The attentional state records the objects, properties, and relations that are salient at each point of the discourse.

The distinction among the linguistic structure, the intentional structure, and the attentional state is essential to provide an adequate explanation of cue phrases, referring expressions, and interruptions.
This theory provides a framework for describing the processing of utterances in a discourse.
Discourse processing requires recognizing how the utterances of the discourse aggregate into segments.
entities: theory of attention , intention , and aggregation of utterances
